# source: tikz-cd's manual (tikz-cd-doc, v1.0): §1 getting started (the
# tikzcd environment as a matrix of math cells, & and \\, \arrow and its
# alias \ar with a direction of r, l, u and d letters, the quotes label
# syntax with ' for swap, and the alternative syntax \arrow{direction}{label}
# with its optional label bracket), §2 controlling the appearance (row sep,
# column sep and sep by name — tiny, small, scriptsize, normal, large, huge —
# or by length; ampersand replacement; the arrow style keys rightarrow and
# the rest; dashed; colours; description labels; \tikzcdset), §3 advanced
# usage (bend left and bend right, start anchor and end anchor, shift left
# and shift right, crossing over, phantom, marking, to= and from=, cell
# options |[...]|). A diagram standing alone in a display is drawn by the
# engine's diagram reader where it reads every key (tikzlibrarycd.code.tex's
# matrix and arrow semantics); a key it does not read routes the diagram
# whole to the graphics boundary (N0023), and where no tool draws it — these
# probes fulfil nothing — the request is withdrawn and the reader's drawing
# ships with the key named, so those rows are refusals.
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \ar[r] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, "f"] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, "f"'] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, "f" description] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[d] \\ B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[dr] & \\ & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A & B \arrow[l] \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \\ B \arrow[u] \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow{r}{f} & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow{r}[swap]{f} & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow{r} & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \rar & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A & B \lar \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \dar \\ B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \\ B \uar \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \drar & \\ & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} & A \dlar \\ B & \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} & B \\ A \urar & \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} B & \\ & A \ular \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=large] A \arrow[d] \\ B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=small] A \arrow[r] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd}[sep=huge] A \arrow[r] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2em] A \arrow[r] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&] A \arrow[r] \& B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, red] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, dashed] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, bend left] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, bend right=40] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, start anchor=north east, end anchor=north west] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, phantom, "\cong"] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body impl \begin{equation*}\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r] & B \end{tikzcd}\end{equation*}
body impl \begin{align*}\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r] & B \end{tikzcd}\end{align*}
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, hook] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, two heads] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, maps to] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, Rightarrow] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, equal] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, shift left] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, shift right] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[to=Z] & |[alias=Z]| B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, from=Z] & |[alias=Z]| B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} |[red]| A \arrow[r] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \tikzcdset{arrow style=tikz}\[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, crossing over] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd}[cramped] A \arrow[r] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, squiggly] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
body refuse:W0334 \[\begin{tikzcd} A \arrow[r, "f" marking] & B \end{tikzcd}\]
pre impl \tikzcdset{arrow style=tikz}
# \tikzcdset lines are the boundary's: the command is read and carried to
# the boundary's standalone (the pre row), and a diagram in a document that
# sets them is drawn there, or natively with the settings named where no
# tool draws it (the body row with its diagram, a refusal). A cell's own
# |[...]| options and the to= and from= targets they name are refusals the
# same way: named, never set as the cell's mathematics.
